newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil Range, union to meet conciliator.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range, union to meet conciliator.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp said on Thursday the union representing workers at the Faro lead and zinc operation in Canada's Yukon has called in a conciliator to help the union and company settle on a labor contract.

About 350 of 420 employees at the site are unionized, but about 300 of those have been laid off since the mine was temporarily shut down last December, Anvil Range's chief financial officer, Victor Wells told Reuters.
However, the mill at Faro, which produces about 12,500 tonnes of ore daily, is still operating.
The ore has been grading an averaging of three percent zinc and two percent lead, Wells said. "The negotiations are down to the nitty-gritty," he said. "They're very positive."
He said the main issue to be resolved was money.
The union is involved in putting together a plan to restructure the mine operations, Wells added.

The company is currently revising its mining plan and is developing new plans to operate and finance its lead and zinc mine at Faro. The plans will not be ready for another three or four weeks and a decision on whether to reopen the mine cannot be made until the plans are finished, Wells said.
"I remain optimistic," Wells said. "There are a lot of things in our favor right now."
Rising zinc prices have been encouraging, he added.
Anvil Range recently raised C$9.4 million through a share issue with Cominco Ltd.
But the company will need to raise an additional C$20 million or C$30 million, Wells said.
"The money from Cominco certainly helps," he said. "But we still need more."
